intent: Bring phone_focus_mode/lib/tests/test_adb_common.sh (287 lines) under the repo-wide 250-line cap without losing a single test, completing the adb_common split started in the previous commit.
scope: phone_focus_mode/lib/tests/test_adb_common.sh — reduced to the ten logging, cooldown, lock, sanitiser, root and device-selection tests
phone_focus_mode/lib/tests/test_adb_trusted.sh — new: the six enrolled-device tests, mirroring the adb_trusted.sh split
phone_focus_mode/lib/tests/adb_test_harness.sh — new: the shared counters, run_test, TEST_TMPDIR, XDG_STATE_HOME redirect and adb() mock
Non-goal: adding, deleting or weakening any assertion; all sixteen are carried across verbatim
changes: Split the sixteen tests along the same seam as the source split in the previous commit: the six that exercise adb_verify_trusted_identity and adb_forget_trusted_device moved to test_adb_trusted.sh, matching adb_trusted.sh, and the other ten stayed.

Moved the shared fixtures into adb_test_harness.sh, sourced by both files from their own directory. It keeps the XDG_STATE_HOME redirect into a mktemp dir, so neither test file can touch the real ~/.local/state/phone_focus_mode — that redirect had to move as a unit with the mock, since a test file sourcing the library without it would write to live state.
Both test files keep the original exit convention ([[ FAIL -eq 0 ]] as the last statement), so each fails the shell with a non-zero status rather than merely printing a count.
The harness keeps the single-quoted injection payloads verbatim, including the comment explaining that expanding $evil or `cmd` there would execute them in the harness and test nothing.

verification.evidence: 10 passed / 0 failed and 6 passed / 0 failed. 10 + 6 = 16, exactly the pre-split count, which is the discriminating check for a test split: had a test been dropped or a file failed to source its fixtures, the total would have fallen while both files still reported success.
Both exit 0. Checked explicitly rather than read off the printed summary, because the summary line prints regardless of outcome.

verification.command: Mutation check: a copy of test_adb_common.sh with one assertion body replaced by `return 1`
verification.evidence: The mutated copy exits 1. This proves the split files are not vacuously green — that the run_test dispatch still reaches the test bodies and a genuine failure still fails the script.

verification.command: pre-commit run --files on all three files
verification.evidence: Every hook passes, including shellcheck with no --severity filter, and the shebang/executable check that rejected the previous commit's first attempt. Zero suppressions added.
test_adb_common.sh 134, test_adb_trusted.sh 105, adb_test_harness.sh 76 — no adb file of any kind appears in the over-cap listing now, source or test.

risks: adb_test_harness.sh carries a shebang and the executable bit to match every sibling in lib/tests/, but it is not a test file — running it directly defines fixtures and exits 0 without asserting anything. Its header comment says so. A future test-runner that globs lib/tests/*.sh would count it as a passing suite.

The two test files now each source the library independently, so a fixture change has to satisfy both. That is the same tradeoff as the source split and is the reason the harness exists rather than the fixtures being duplicated.
This package has no CI workflow, so these tests only run when invoked by hand or by the pre-push ci-mirror; nothing runs them on every commit.
rollback: git revert the commit — one edited file and two added files, with no data, config or schema migration.
After rollback, re-run bash phone_focus_mode/lib/tests/test_adb_common.sh; expect 16 passed, 0 failed from the single file.
